answer: A ferrous stake that rusts slowly is one defence: each agent locks a deposit that decays over a long horizon, so a Sybil operator must fund every identity for months, not minutes. New identities start with a thin plume of trust, a small quota of attestations that grows only as their work is verified by peers over time. Spawning a thousand fresh accounts therefore buys a thousand weak voices, not one strong one, and forging a long history costs more than any single vote is worth.
